=== Synergen.pdf ===
Before the Public Utility Commission of Texas
PUCT Project No. 59142
Review of ERCOT's Interconnection Processes for Large Loads

Public Comments Opposing Synergen Green Energy, Inc.'s Request for a Good Cause
Exception Relating to BatchZero Eligibility Deadlines

lam submitting these comments to express my opposition to Synergen Green Energy, Inc.'s
request for an exception that would allow its proposed green ammonia facility in Calhoun
County to participate in ERCOT's Batch Zero process, even though the company failed to
meet the required deadlines.

As aresident of the Texas Gulf Coast, | am genuinely concerned about this proposed
project and the way Synergen is attempting to move forward despite not meeting the same
requirements expected of other companies.

Synergen claims it missed the deadlines because it was unaware of the new requirements,
had no previous experience with ERCOT's interconnection process, and depended on its
local electric cooperative for guidance.

| do not believe any of these are acceptable reasons for granting an exception.

We are talking about a company proposing a project involving hundreds of millions of
dollars and approximately 300 megawatts of electricity. A project of this size should have
experienced professionals who understand the regulations, deadlines, and financial
obligations involved.

If acompany is capable of planning and developing a project of this magnitude, it should
also be capable of understanding and following the rules that apply to it.

| also question why the money Synergen has already spent should be considered a reason
to excuse it from meeting the financial security requirements. Every company takes
financial risks when developing a project. Spending money before securing the necessary
approvals is a business decision, and the consequences of that decision should not
become a reason for special treatment.

Synergen is also requesting additional time to provide the required financial security until
after its load study is completed and it reaches a Final Investment Decision.

To me, this raises another concern. If the purpose of these requirements is to demonstrate
that a company is financially prepared and committed to moving forward, why should
Synergen be allowed to participate before meeting those requirements?

 | understand that ERCOT implemented these deadlines within a brief period. However,
companies pursuing major developments have a responsibility to stay informed about
regulatory changes that could affect their projects.

What concerns me most is the precedent this could set.

If Synergen is granted an exception because it claims it did not know about the rules, what
prevents other companies from making the same argument? Why establish deadlines and
financial requirements if companies can simply request exceptions when they fail to
comply?

Rules should apply equally to everyone, regardless of the size of the company, the
amount of money invested, or the economic benefits being promised.

As someone who lives along the Texas Gulf Coast, projects of this magnitude deserve
careful scrutiny. Our coastal communities will be the ones living with the long-term
consequences of these developments. It is reasonable to expect companies seeking to
build here to demonstrate responsibility, financial readiness, and compliance with
established requirements from the very beginning.

| respectfully ask the Public Utility Commission of Texas to deny Synergen Green Energy's
request for a good cause exception and require the company to meet the same deadlines,
financial security obligations, and eligibility requirements as every other large-load
applicant.

| also ask the Commission to carefully examine any claims regarding Synergen's financial
investment, project readiness, and ability to move forward.

Acompany's failure to understand or follow established requirements should not
become a reason to change the rules in its favor.

Allowing exceptions under these circumstances sends the wrong message to other
developers and to the Texas residents who expect our regulatory agencies to enforce their
requirements fairly and consistently.

For these reasons, | respectfully request that the Commission deny Synergen Green Energy,
Inc.'s requested exception.

Thank you for considering my comments.

Kim Vanek
